messages.content: Calculate the slope gradient in degree between two points on a landscape with coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437).

function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m happy to help, but I’ll need a bit more information to compute a slope gradient.

A slope gradient (in degrees, percent, or ratio) is defined as the change in elevation divided by the horizontal distance between two points:

\[
\text{slope} = \frac{\Delta \text{elevation}}{\text{horizontal distance}}
\]

From the coordinates you provided – (40.7128 N, –74.0060 W) and (34.0522 N, –118.2437 W) – we can calculate the horizontal (great‑circle) distance between the two locations, but we don’t have the elevations at those points. Without the elevation difference (\(\Delta \text{elevation}\)), the slope gradient cannot be determined.

If you can supply the elevations (or the vertical difference) for each point, I can plug them into the formula and give you the slope gradient in degrees. Alternatively, if you’re looking for the great‑circle bearing or the central angle between the two points, let me know and I can compute that instead.
